chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abi Ishaq who linked it up to Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: There are three signs for the wasteful one: He eats what is not his (deserved), he wears what is not his (deserved), and he buys what is not his (deserved).

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.المسرف: The wasteful one / one who exceeds bounds in spending or consumption

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of a wasteful person according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the wasteful person (*al-musrif*) not merely by excess, but by the illegitimacy of their acquisition—eating, wearing, and buying what is not rightfully theirs. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *haqq* (right/entitlement), where true ownership is tied to spiritual merit and divine permission rather than mere physical possession. The hadith serves as a practical ethical guide, urging believers to evaluate their material consumption through the lens of piety and justice.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-45 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Abi Ishaq who linked it up to Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB) ,
“There are three signs for one who is wasteful: What he eats, he doesn’t deserve to eat; what he wears, he doesn’t deserve to wear, and what he buys, he doesn’t deserve to buy.”
